title.narrative: Activity under preparation Continued Support to International Economic Integration of Timor-Leste

description.narrative: The proposed action supports Timor-Leste's deeper economic integration in Southeast Asia and the global economy. It constitutes the second phase of an existing programme that has been instrumental in Timor-Leste¿s WTO and ASEAN accession processes, gaining the EU a prominent position vis-à-vis government counterparts. Framed and implemented as a Global Gateway 360-degree action, it aims to combine policy dialogue, technical assistance, capacity building, and investment facilitation to deliver coordinated, values-based, and long-term impact in economic governance and the economy. The overall goal is to foster sustainable economic development, inclusive and gender responsive job creation, and higher income through increased investment, productivity, and economic diversification. The action proposes to leverage Timor-Leste¿s WTO, ASEAN and (potential) EPA membership to strengthen public sector capacity and improve its business environment by aligning policy and legal frameworks with international standards. It will also enhance private sector¿s ability to benefit from new economic opportunities and facilitate civil society engagement. The action will be implemented in indirect management with an entrusted entity(ies), which will be selected by the Commission¿s services using the following criteria in 4.3.1. Based on the experience and trust gained through the ongoing project Support to Regional Integration and Trade, and contingent on successful negotiations, the International Trade Centre will be considered as entrusted entity. Stakeholders involve various ministries, parliament, and the private sector. Inclusive engagement with persons living in vulnerable situations and civil society is emphasised to ensure broad ownership. Risks include political instability, institutional weaknesses, an underdeveloped private sector, poor infrastructure, and external shocks. The action aims to mitigate these through good governance, consultations, and strategic use of national policy space.
